note: Attacker-controlled 'stringOffset' from the name table header is dereferenced to form the string-pool pointer passed into record serialization; no per-record bounds validation guards it.

Root cause: sanitize validates only the records array and 'stringOffset', but never checks each record's 'offset'+'length' against the string pool, so malformed name records pass sanitization and later reads escape the buffer.
The record's unvalidated 'offset' and 'length' fields select the byte range to read from the string pool (src_base).

code: out->arrayZ[i] = arrayZ[i]; /* TODO: add version that calls c->copy() */
note: Sink: 'length' bytes are copied from src_base+offset; when offset+length exceeds the pool (and the file), the loop reads past the input buffer into uninitialized memory.
